reproResult: Followed the "Minimal reproduction" in my own worktree at 16ceb3a54 (own dev instance app :14231 / server :22231 / daemon :30231, fresh fixture, new project proj_zfaz9fujtc, thread thr_5wvm6uxwjk with one codex turn). All three surfaces reproduce with numbers identical to the report: (A) step4 → td=50000, th=601, tableNodes=101306, bodyRows=500, columns=100, scroll size 28848x14529 px in a 507x744 box, 4.9 s from Enter to table; step5 (dev build, 4x CPU throttle) longest task 14001 ms, total 23339 ms (report: 13721 / 24220). (B) step2 → 5000 <li> / 20000 elements in a 128 px max-h-32 box, scrollHeight 120008, and DOM element count identical before and after expanding the banner (20587), confirming the collapsed banner keeps the list mounted; GET /environments/<id>/status returned 200 with 425343 bytes and workspace.workingTree.files.length=5000 (byte-identical size to the report). (C) step6 → 5000 <li> in the h-56 (224 px) box, scrollHeight 132821, 20001 elements. The jsdom vitest file passes (2/2) as the report says. Deviations needed: (1) the spawn command as written (`BB_SERVER_URL=... pnpm bb:dev thread spawn ...`) failed with "HTTP 404: Host not found" because BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT was inherited from the outer shell (points at the user's real daemon); it worked once BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT was also set (i.e. `eval "$(scripts/bb-dev-app env)"`). (2) step6 timed out on `waitUntil: "networkidle"` when run after step4 on the same persistent dev-browser page (the 50k-cell CSV tab is still open); it worked on a fresh page against the app root. (3) /tmp was at 98% inode usage on this host so I placed the fixture under /home instead of /tmp (environmental, not a report defect). Root-cause excerpts (FilePreview.tsx L209-210, L971-995; WorkspaceChangesList.tsx L98-119; ThreadPromptContextBanner.tsx L660-687, L1148-1163; RemotePathBrowser.tsx L240-262, L385-390; host-files.ts L150-183; workspace.ts porcelain map; resource-pagination.tsx L306-309; command.tsx L54-64; the limit constants) all match the files at 16ceb3a54. Nothing on origin/main after the base touches these files (fe230cd3d touches ThreadBackgroundCommandsCard, not the banner). Screenshots are real 1400x900 PNGs matching their captions; all linked repro artifacts exist. Related issues #1616/#1301/#1261(closed)/#1749 exist with the described titles.

findings.problem: The spawn command sets only BB_SERVER_URL; if the shell already has BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT (as any shell launched from a bb thread does, pointing at the user's real daemon :38887), the CLI resolves the local host id from the wrong daemon and the server replies 'HTTP 404: Host not found'. A clueless reader following the step literally in this environment cannot create the thread.
findings.evidence: Ran `BB_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:22231 pnpm bb:dev thread spawn --project proj_zfaz9fujtc --provider codex ...` → `Error: Failed to create thread: HTTP 404: Host not found` (env had BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT=38887). Re-ran with `BB_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:22231 BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT=30231 ...` → thread thr_5wvm6uxwjk created. apps/cli/src/daemon.ts resolveLocalHostId() → fetchLocalHostId uses BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT; packages/scripts/src/commands/run-cli.ts only fills it from devEnv when unset.
findings.fix: Replace the env prefix in steps 3 and the Appendix with `eval "$(scripts/bb-dev-app env)"` (or add BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT=<daemon port>) before `pnpm bb:dev thread spawn`, and note that the host id must come from your own instance's /api/v1/hosts.

findings.problem: The report says step5-measure-csv.js and step5b-measure-csv-prod.js produce '1x then 4x' results, but the saved scripts end with only `await measure(4);`, and step5.out / step5b.out contain interleaved Playwright timeout / 'Target page closed' error traces between the 1x and 4x lines, so the artifacts don't correspond to a single clean run of the scripts as saved.
findings.evidence: grep 'measure(' repro/step5*.js → only `await measure(4);` at line 43/48; repro/step5.out and step5b.out include 'TimeoutError: ... waiting for getByRole(button, { name: /Show right panel/ })' and 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. My run of the saved step5 script printed only the 4x line (maxLongTaskMs 14001, total 23339 — consistent with the report's 4x numbers).
findings.fix: Either make the scripts run measure(1) then measure(4) as documented, or state that the 1x line came from a separate invocation; strip or explain the error traces in the .out files.

findings.problem: Scripts share the persistent dev-browser page 'main'; after step4 leaves the 50,000-cell CSV tab open, step6's `page.goto(..., { waitUntil: "networkidle" })` timed out (30 s) and a retry was 'interrupted by another navigation'. The report does not warn about running order or page reuse.
findings.evidence: v2-step6 run 1: 'TimeoutError: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... waiting until networkidle'; run 2 with waitUntil:'load': 'Navigation ... is interrupted by another navigation'; run 3 on a fresh page ('p6') against the app root succeeded: rows=5000, boxH=224, scrollH=132821. The author's own step6.out shows nodesBefore=122048, i.e. they ran it on the heavy CSV page and got lucky.
findings.fix: Have step6 open a fresh page (browser.newPage()) at the app root and/or use waitUntil:'load'; mention that step scripts can be run independently.

findings.problem: Report says CommandList 'has no consumers' / 'no file in apps/app imports it'. The apps/app statement is true, but the shared-ui CommandList is used by plugins/tasks (rail.tsx, new-task-dialog.tsx). The refutation itself still stands (CommandList maps nothing; it is a container), but the 'unused' wording is inaccurate.
findings.fix: Change 'unused container / no consumers' to 'a container primitive that maps nothing (used only by the tasks plugin's cmdk pickers, which hold small lists)'.

findings.problem: Small readability nits for a clueless reader: the status payload field is described as `workingTree.files.length` but the JSON path is `workspace.workingTree.files`; the fixture is placed on /tmp, which on this host is a tmpfs near inode exhaustion (5,047 inodes per fixture copy) — worth a one-line note since the repro creates 5,000 files.
findings.evidence: python: json keys of env-status.json → ['outcome','workspace']; /workspace/workingTree/files len 5000. `df -i /tmp` → 98% inodes used before I created the fixture (first attempt failed with ENOSPC).
findings.fix: Write the exact JSON path and add a note that the fixture can live anywhere on a non-tmpfs disk (the path only needs to be an absolute path readable by the host daemon).
